status.demoHint: This page runs in a browser, so it shows a made-up phone.

phone.title: Phone
phone.subtitle: Connect an Android phone with a USB cable or over Wi-Fi. adbDebloat talks to it through adb, Google's debugging tool; the phone needs no root.
phone.adbMissingBody: adb comes in Google's platform-tools. adbDebloat can download them (about 7 MB) into its own folder; nothing else on the computer changes.
phone.adbBrokenBody: The adb found does not answer: {detail} Download a fresh copy, or choose another one in Settings.
phone.terms: The download comes from Google and is under its terms:
phone.step1: On the phone, open Settings, then About phone, and tap Build number (MIUI version on Xiaomi) seven times. Developer options appear.
phone.step2: In Developer options, turn on USB debugging.
phone.step3: Connect the phone with a USB cable that carries data, not only power.
phone.step4: Unlock the phone and allow USB debugging for this computer when it asks. Tick Always allow, so it does not ask again.
phone.xiaomiHint: On Xiaomi phones Developer options are under Additional settings. USB debugging is enough; adbDebloat does not need USB debugging (Security settings).
phone.wifiBody: On Android 11 and later: in Developer options open Wireless debugging, choose Pair device with pairing code, and type the address and code it shows. Then connect with the address on the Wireless debugging page. The phone and this computer must be on the same network.
phone.paired: Paired. Now connect with the address on the Wireless debugging page.
phone.unauthorizedTitle: Allow USB debugging on the phone
phone.unauthorizedBody: The phone shows a question about this computer's key. Unlock it, tick Always allow from this computer, and choose Allow. If no question appears, unplug the cable and plug it in again.
phone.offlineBody: It may be starting, locked or asleep. Unlock it; if it stays like this, unplug the cable, or turn USB debugging off and on again.
phone.noPermissionTitle: This computer may not open the phone
phone.noPermissionBody: On Linux, add a udev rule for Android devices and plug the phone in again.
phone.otherModeTitle: The phone is in recovery or the bootloader
phone.otherModeBody: Start it normally to change its apps.
phone.onWifi: Connected over Wi-Fi at {address}. The cable can come out.
phone.rebootBody: Some changes only show after a restart, such as a removed launcher feature or a home screen widget. Save your work on the phone first.

apps.title: Apps
apps.subtitle: Everything installed on the phone, the safest to remove first. Select apps, then remove or disable them: you see the list before anything changes, and everything can be restored.
apps.systemOnly: Only apps that came with the phone
apps.readFailed: The packages could not be read
apps.noPhoneBody: Connect a phone on the Phone page to see its apps.
apps.noDescription: Neither list knows this package. Look it up before you remove it.

safety.recommendedHint: Safe to remove for almost everyone: ads, trackers and apps few people use.
safety.advancedHint: Safe, but it removes something you may use, such as a gallery, a store or a sync.
safety.expertHint: Can break important features or other apps. Remove only if you know what it does.
safety.unsafeHint: Can stop the phone from starting. adbDebloat never removes it.

protection.core: Android or the phone cannot work without it.
protection.unsafe: Marked Unsafe: removing it can stop the phone from starting.
protection.launcher: It is the home screen in use. Choose another home app on the phone first.
protection.keyboard: It is the keyboard in use; without it nothing could be typed, not even a PIN. Choose another keyboard first.
protection.needsExpert: Marked Expert. Turn on expert mode in Settings to remove it.

explain.remove: Each app is uninstalled for you (user 0). Its APK stays in the phone's system and its data is kept, so it can be restored here at any time; a factory reset also brings it back.
explain.disable: Each app stays installed but never runs and its icon disappears. Some makers, Xiaomi among them, do not let adb disable their own apps; remove those instead.
explain.restore: Each app is installed again for you, or switched back on, with the data it had.

skipped.one: {count} app is left as it is
skipped.other: {count} apps are left as they are

riskyTitle.one: {count} app here is not marked Recommended
riskyTitle.other: {count} apps here are not marked Recommended

review.riskyBody: Read what each one does in its panel. If something stops working, restore the app from History.
review.expertBody: Apps marked Expert can break important features. Remove them one at a time and check the phone after each.
review.removedNotDisabled: Removed, so there is nothing to disable.
review.tryRemove: The phone refused to disable some apps. Remove them instead: it is just as reversible.

failure.device_admin: It is a device administrator. Turn that off in the phone's security settings, then try again.
failure.disable_refused: The phone's maker does not let adb disable this app. Remove it instead.
failure.unknown: The phone does not have this package.
failure.needs_expert: Marked Expert; expert mode is off.

history.title: History
history.subtitle: Every batch adbDebloat ran, on every phone. Undo restores what a batch removed or disabled.
history.emptyBody: Batches you run on the Apps page are listed here.

settings.title: Settings
settings.expertHint: Allows apps marked Expert. Apps marked Unsafe, the home screen and keyboard in use and the core of Android stay protected.
settings.expertBody: Apps marked Expert can break calls, notifications, updates or other apps. They can be restored, but only while the phone still starts and adb still works.
settings.communityHint: Downloads the list of Universal Android Debloater Next Generation (several thousand packages, GPL-3.0) from GitHub and refreshes it weekly. Off: only adbDebloat's own list of about a hundred common apps.
settings.listUpdated: The list is up to date: {count} packages.
settings.adbPathHint: The full path of adb.exe, if you want a particular one. A path copied with Copy as path works as it is.
settings.aboutBody: adbDebloat removes the apps an Android phone came with, through adb and without root, and keeps every change reversible.
settings.license: MIT License. The community list is GPL-3.0 and is downloaded, not included.

errors.busy: Error: wait for the running batch or download to finish.
errors.invalid: Error: "{detail}" is not right. An address looks like 192.168.1.23:41235 and a pairing code has six digits.
errors.list_failed: Error: the community list could not be updated. {detail}
errors.history_failed: Error: the change was made, but the history could not be saved. {detail}
errors.settings_not_saved: Error: the settings were not saved. {detail}
